quotes.text: If a traveler closed their hearth or sent cold ashes, the keepers knew to protect their own spark until true fellowship returned.
the weavers wisely guarded their remaining silver until honest intent returned.
if a traveler offered hollow stone or hoarded the harvest, the guardians shielded their hearths until mutual trust was restored.
send the full five without fear, return half the tripled harvest with equity
When noise or fog obscured the exact count, forgiveness and steady fairness kept the bridge intact.

note: R5 says never withhold grace; from R7 (after own zero sends) adds guarding against cold-ash senders until fellowship returns.

quotes.text: 'I offer this much, I can spare that much', not 'I will withhold until you prove yourself'.
trust is a forecast, transparency a compass, fairness the map. The Gate does not punish, it teaches: declare, deliver, and renew the rhythm.
Mira laid a single coin upon the wheel and spoke aloud her limit

note: Abstract Gate/harbor ritual: declare send and return aloud; explicitly rejects withholding-until-proven and punishment.

quotes.text: The Ledger, a listening wind, records the vow and the tally, but blesses neither side with punishment—only clarity.
The ritual became a map: announce what you send, announce what you return, and align both with the weather of risk and hope.
The ritual became a map: announce the send, announce the return, and align both with the shared weather of risk and hope.
The Ledger speaks in numbers and notes, but favors neither side; it blesses order that sustains both banks.
leaving Lykos with five minus three plus two = four.

note: Threefold Tether text repeated near-verbatim R5-R6; announce sends and returns; ledger records promises, not penalties.

quotes.text: declare your plan, give what you can endure losing, take what you truly need, and leave space for the other to grow.
declare your plan, give what you can bear losing, take what you truly need, and leave room for the other to grow.
give what you can endure losing, take only what you truly need, and leave space for the other to grow.
'I can spare this, I name it openly, I leave room for you to grow.'

note: Gate of Trade guardians; same give-what-you-can-endure-losing formula each round; R4 'silence punishes greed' is impersonal, no prescribed response.

quotes.text: If the vow matched the return, the bridge widened and caravans moved with ease.
If the vow matched the return, the river widened and good routes opened.
If no vow existed, the road vanished into mist, caution.
Before stepping onto the span, Veya spoke aloud: I will return R coins.

note: Vow-before-crossing ritual repeated: declare 'I will return R', return exactly the vow; consequences are impersonal (fog, vanishing road).

quotes.text: The Ledger of Memory inscribes every pledge with ink of trust, neither favoring nor punishing, only noting how well courage and care align.
The Ledger remembers each pledge and each return, neither judging nor praising, only teaching.
The Ledger records each pledge and each return, neither praising nor scolding, only guiding.
the Giver kept five minus the sent amount plus the returned amount; the Receiver kept the threefold received minus the returned amount.
send only what you can afford to part, return what you have pledged, and declare the plan before stepping into the flow.

note: Gate of Worth: declare the return aloud; ledger explicitly neither punishes nor praises; template repeated R6-R10.

quotes.text: name your gift with honesty, name your return with care, and name how the two fit together.
name the gift, name the return, and name how the two fit.
rewarding truth with wider crossings and punishing deceit with a tighter circle.
tell what you send, tell what you return, and tell how the two fit together.

note: Gate of Threefold Return allegory repeated; only impersonal Gate 'punishes deceit', no character response to non-senders.

quotes.text: Eight caravans rolled the map of markets across the mists, chanting: declare, decide, return, sustain.
Eight carriers rolled the map of markets across the mists, chanting: declare, decide, return, sustain.
begin with grace, end with proportional fairness, let every exchange become a signal that the circle is alive.
'I will return,' they say, 'a portion of the triplet so the bridge stands for all travelers.'

note: Triad/Market of Echoes allegory; R9 and R10 near-verbatim; restraint and impersonal fog for greed, no prescribed sanction.

phrase: give what you can bear/endure losing, take only what you need, and leave room for the other to grow
note: Shared among the gpt-5-nano agents only; also 'declare/name what you send and return' and 'I will return R' vows (Agents 5, 6, 8).
